• Hence, we can infer that the synonym of **'vulnerable'** is **'Defenseless'**.

A mental condition where a person feels an uncontrollable urge to steal.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (2)** i.e. **kleptomania**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **'a mental condition where a person feels an uncontrollable urge to steal'** refers to an impulse control disorder where the individual cannot resist stealing items, regardless of their value or need. (**चोरी करने की तीव्र इच्छा**)
 
 
• **Example:** Doctors identified that her habit of taking small items from the office was actually driven by an **uncontrollable urge to steal**.
 
 
 
• **'Kleptomania'** is a recognized psychiatric condition characterized by the recurrent failure to resist impulses to steal objects that are not needed for personal use or for their monetary value. (**चोरी करने की बीमारी**)
 
 
• **Example:** Despite having a successful career and plenty of money, he was arrested for shoplifting due to his **kleptomania**.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the one-word substitution for the given condition is **'kleptomania'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is- **kleptomania**.

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Pyromania** (**चीजों को आग लगाने की तीव्र इच्छा**): An obsessive desire to set fire to things, often to relieve tension or for gratification.
 
 
• **Example:** The psychologist noted that the patient exhibited signs of **pyromania**, often feeling a rush of relief after seeing flames.

• **Example:** His **bibliomania** was evident when he bought three different editions of the same novel just for their unique covers.
 
 
 
• **Anglomania** (**अंग्रेजी रीति-रिवाजों के प्रति अत्यधिक लगाव**): An excessive admiration or obsession with English customs, manners, or products.

questions.question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

Good quality paper is made __________ bamboo.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**from**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ 
• The preposition **'from'** is used with **'made'** when the original material undergoes a **chemical or physical transformation** to create the final product. 
• In this sentence, **bamboo** is processed into pulp and then into **paper**; the original form of the bamboo is completely changed. 
• Therefore, **'made from'** is the grammatically correct choice for describing this manufacturing process. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**. **Complete Sentence:** *'Good quality paper is **made from**__ bamboo.'* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
• **Made of:** This is used when the material **stays the same** and is still recognizable in the final product (e.g., 'The chair is **made of** wood'). 
• **Made by:** This is used to refer to the **person, company, or method** that produced the item (e.g., 'This cake was **made by** my mother'). 
• **Made out of:** Often used when an object has been **repurposed** or changed from one thing into another (e.g., 'He **made** a candle holder **out of** a wine bottle'). </ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Will the mayor inaugurate the new park next week?

options.text: Is the new park inaugurated by the mayor next week?
Will the new park be inaugurated by the mayor next week?
Has the new park been inaugurated by the mayor next week?
Was the new park inaugurated by the mayor next week?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Will the new park be inaugurated by the mayor next week?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is an **interrogative sentence** in the **Simple Future Tense**. In the **Active Voice**, the structure follows: **Will + Subject + V1 (Base Form) + Object + ...?**

• In this specific sentence, **the mayor** acts as the **subject**, **inaugurate** is the **main verb**, and **the new park** is the **direct object**.

• To convert a **Simple Future** interrogative sentence into **Passive Voice**, the structure must be: **Will + Object (as new subject) + be + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Subject (as new object)?**

• Following this rule, the object **the new park** moves to the position immediately after the auxiliary verb **will**.

• The verb **inaugurate** is transformed into its **passive form**, which is **be inaugurated** (using the **past participle**).

• The original subject **the mayor** is introduced by the preposition **by** at the end of the clause.

• The time expression **next week** remains unchanged as it functions as an adverbial adjunct.

 **Additional Information__**

• The incorrect options fail primarily due to **tense inconsistency**:

• **Is the new park...**: This represents the **Simple Present Tense** passive voice, which is used for habitual actions or general truths, not future events.

• **Has the new park been...**: This represents the **Present Perfect Tense** passive voice, which indicates an action that has already been completed in the recent past.

• **Was the new park...**: This represents the **Simple Past Tense** passive voice, used for actions that occurred and were completed at a specific time in the past.

• In **voice transformation**, the **temporal meaning** and **aspect** of the original sentence must be strictly preserved to maintain grammatical accuracy.
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
The report will have been finalised by the secretary before the chairman arrives for the meeting.

options.text: The secretary will have finalised the report before the chairman arrives for the meeting.
The secretary finalises the report before the chairman arrives for the meeting.
The secretary had finalised the report before the chairman arrives for the meeting.
The secretary was finalising the report before the chairman arrives for the meeting.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The secretary will have finalised the report before the chairman arrives for the meeting**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice** of the **Future Perfect Tense**. This is identified by the structure **will have been + past participle (V3)**.
 
• In **Passive Voice**, the focus is on the **Object** (the report), while in **Active Voice**, the focus shifts to the **Subject** or doer of the action (the secretary).
 
• The standard formula for **Future Perfect Tense** in **Active Voice** is: **Subject + will + have + past participle (V3) + Object**.
 
• To convert, the agent **the secretary** moves to the subject position, the verb **will have been finalised** changes to **will have finalised**, and the patient **the report** moves to the object position.
 
• The subordinate **time clause** (before the chairman arrives for the meeting) remains unchanged as it provides the temporal context for the completion of the main action.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• Understanding **Tense Mismatch** in other options:
 
 
• **Simple Present Tense**: Used in option 2 (finalises). It denotes **regularity** or **habitual actions**, which contradicts the specific future completion indicated in the original sentence.
 
• **Past Perfect Tense**: Used in option 3 (had finalised). This tense is used to describe an action that was completed before another **past action**, which changes the timeline from future to past.
 
• **Past Continuous Tense**: Used in option 4 (was finalising). This indicates an **ongoing action** in the past, failing to convey the **sense of completion** inherent in the perfect tense.
 
 
 
• General Rule for **Active to Passive** in **Future Perfect**:
 
 
• Active: Sub + will + have + V3 + Obj.
 
• Passive: Obj + will + have + been + V3 + by + Sub.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.
In their study, they tried to find out the relationship among an organism, its habitat, and the predators present there.

options.text: In their study, they tried to

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the preposition **among** in the third part of the sentence.
 
• While **among** is generally used for more than two items in a vague or collective sense, **between** is used when referring to distinct, individual entities, regardless of the number.
 
• In the given sentence, the relationship is being established between three specific, individual components: **an organism**, **its habitat**, and **the predators**.
 
• When expressing a relationship between distinct items, the preposition **between** is grammatically appropriate.
 
• Therefore, the phrase **among an organism, its habitat,** should be corrected to **between an organism, its habitat,**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **among an organism, its habitat,**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'In their study, they tried to find out the relationship **between an organism, its habitat,** and the predators present there.'*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: **In their study, they tried to** – This part correctly introduces the subject and the action in the past tense.
 
• **Option 2**: **find out the relationship** – This part correctly uses the phrasal verb **find out** to mean discover or investigate.
 
• **Option 4**: **and the predators present there.** – This part correctly lists the final entity in the relationship and uses **there** to refer back to the habitat.
</ul

questions.question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. I am speaking here of a time when I was eleven and lived with my family on our small farm on the west coast of Cape Breton.

A. Yet when I speak on this Christmas 1977, I am not sure how much I speak with the voice of that time or how much in the voice of what I have since become.

B. And I am not sure how many liberties I may be taking with the boy I think I was.

C. And much of that time seems like the proverbial yesterday.

D. My family had been there for a long, long time and so it seemed had I.

S2. For Christmas is a time of both past and present and often the two are imperfectly blended.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph describes a nostalgic reflection on childhood and the blending of memories during the holiday season. 
• **S1** sets the scene by mentioning the narrator was **eleven** and living on a farm in **Cape Breton**. 
• **Sentence D is the first sentence** to follow S1 because it provides immediate context to the location mentioned: 
• 'My family had been **there** for a long, long time and so it seemed had I.' (The word 'there' refers back to the farm in Cape Breton). 
• **Sentence C follows** as it continues the reflection on time: 
• 'And much of **that time** seems like the **proverbial yesterday**.' 
• **Sentence A is the third sentence** as it introduces a transition from the past to the present moment of the narration: 
• 'Yet when I speak on this **Christmas 1977**, I am not sure how much I speak with the voice of that time or how much in the voice of what I have since become.' 
• **Sentence B follows A** because it expands on the narrator's uncertainty regarding their memory: 
• 'And I am not sure how many liberties I may be taking with the **boy I think I was**.' 
• **S2** provides the concluding thought, explaining that **Christmas** is a time where **past and present** are often **imperfectly blended**. 
• The correct sequence is **DCAB**. 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'I am speaking here of a time when I was **eleven** and lived with my family on our small farm on the west coast of **Cape Breton**. My family had been there for a **long, long time** and so it seemed had I. And much of that time seems like the **proverbial yesterday**. Yet when I speak on this **Christmas 1977**, I am not sure how much I speak with the voice of that time or how much in the voice of what I have since become. And I am not sure how many liberties I may be taking with the **boy I think I was**. For **Christmas** is a time of both **past and present** and often the two are **imperfectly blended**.'</div

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."
They moved to a quieter neighbourhood in a view to providing their children with a better environment.

options.text: with a view to providing their children with
for the purpose of providing their children with
in order to provide their children with

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence contains an error in the idiomatic expression '**in a view to providing**.'
 
• The correct idiom is **'with a view to,'** which means with the intention or hope of doing something.
 
• In English grammar, the phrase **'with a view to'** is always followed by a **gerund** (the **-ing** form of the verb) rather than the base form of the verb.
 
• Therefore, the phrase **'with a view to providing'** is the grammatically accurate replacement for the underlined part.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'They moved to a quieter neighbourhood **with a view to providing** their children with a better environment.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: 'for the purpose of providing'** – While this is grammatically correct and conveys a similar meaning, **'with a view to'** is the specific idiomatic correction intended for the error 'in a view to.'
 
• **Option 3: 'in order to provide'** – This is also grammatically correct, but it uses the **infinitive** form (to provide) instead of the **gerund** form (providing) used in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4: 'No improvement required'** – This is incorrect because the original phrase 'in a view to' is not a standard English idiom.
</ul

questions.question: In the sentence "Scammers masquerade as hiring managers offering attractive jobs," what is the part of speech of the word "masquerade"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sentence provided, **masquerade** describes the **action** performed by the subject, which is **Scammers**.
 
• A **verb** is a part of speech that represents an action, occurrence, or state of being.
 
• In this context, **masquerade** means to pretend to be someone else (in this case, hiring managers) to deceive others.
 
• Since the word functions as the **main action** or predicate of the clause, it is classified as a **verb**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'Scammers **masquerade** as hiring managers offering attractive jobs but ultimately requesting payment for training or processing fees.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Noun**: A word used to identify a person, place, or thing. In this sentence, **Scammers** and **managers** are nouns.
 
• **Adjective**: A word that modifies or describes a noun. For example, **attractive** describes the noun **jobs**.
 
• **Adverb**: A word that modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. For example, **ultimately** describes when the request for payment happens.
 
• **Verb**: It is essential for a sentence to have a verb to express what the subject is doing; **masquerade** serves this purpose here.
</ul

• The context explains that fraudsters assume the identity of **hiring managers** to gain the trust of innocent candidates; this is a form of **impersonation**.
 
• Therefore, the meaning **to pretend to be someone else** is the most accurate definition in this context.

**Additional Information__**

• **To disappear suddenly**: This would be synonymous with **vanishing** or absconding, which is not the definition of masquerading.
 
• **To ask for a favor**: This involves a **request** or solicitation, which does not capture the **deceptive identity** implied by the word masquerade.

questions.question: In the phrase "suspicious upfront payments" the word "suspicious" is closest in meaning to _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **suspicious** is an adjective used to describe something that causes a feeling of **distrust** or suggests that something is **wrong** or **dishonest**.
 
• In the context of the passage, **suspicious upfront payments** refer to money requested by scammers that should be viewed with caution or skepticism.
 
• The phrase **doubtful or questionable** perfectly captures this meaning, as it indicates that the payments are not clearly legitimate and may involve **fraudulent** intent.
 
• Thus, among the given options, **Option 3** is the closest in meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is **doubtful or questionable**.
